top_story.description: The day's most consequential network-device story. Usually the item with confirmed exploitation or the widest blast radius.

body.description: 2-4 paragraphs: what happened, which devices, why it matters, what to do first.

ai_section.description: AI and network devices. Only populate when a collected item genuinely concerns AI (AI-assisted attacks or discovery, AI/LLM integrations on network gear, prompt injection against network management). If nothing in today's items qualifies, set has_new_ai to false and leave the other fields empty - the site carries forward the last real one, dated.

vendor.description: Primary vendor, as the vendor writes it: Cisco, Fortinet, Palo Alto Networks, Juniper, F5, Citrix, Ivanti, Check Point, SonicWall, Sophos, HPE Aruba, Arista, MikroTik, Ubiquiti, Zyxel, NETGEAR, TP-Link, D-Link, WatchGuard, Barracuda, Extreme Networks. Use 'Multiple' for several, 'Unspecified' when none is named.

device_types.description: Pick from the fixed list only. A firewall management server is 'management-platform'. A mail or web security appliance is 'other'.

summary.description: One sentence, under 200 characters: what happened and to which device, readable on its own. This is the line someone skims.

vendor_ai_defenses.description: Defensive AI capabilities network vendors offer, as described in this cycle's items: an AI security product or feature, AI-assisted detection or operations, guardrails for AI running on network gear, or a documented vendor approach to defending against AI-enabled attacks. A formal launch is NOT required - a vendor describing a capability it offers counts, and a vendor blog post explaining how its platform handles AI-era threats counts. What does not count is a pure threat report with no defensive offering, and anything not in the sources. Never invent a product name, capability or availability date.

id.description: index of the collected item announcing it

solution.description: Product or capability name exactly as the source names it.

what_it_does.description: One or two sentences, from the source only.

availability.description: GA, preview, announced, described-only, or 'not stated' - use what the source supports.

worth_evaluating_if.description: Which teams should look at it, and why.
